statement: For every negative full once-punctured-torus outer involution, the cusp-reflection fixed subgroup has H1(-,F2)=0 and lies in the full closed commutator subgroup of F. Every actual transporter g with g v g^-1=c v generates the complete fixed rank-one summand of H1(F,Zhat). Every surjective invariant odd cyclic cover has exactly one cycle of cusp reflection sections, and its exact full section counts and fixed-subgroup cohomology are specified. In the identity-modulo-two case, the other full section fixed subgroup maps onto the entire fixed homology line.
depends_on: D43 global negative involution multiplier; D58 full section classes, Bockstein ring and cusp fusion; actual odd cyclic punctured-torus covers and deck averaging over Z2; full-profinite Brown restriction theorem of Kochloukova-Zalesskii, Theorem 2 and Section 1.1; characteristic degree-two Zassenhaus quotient
manuscript_passages: Section 30, folios 194-196, scans 383-387; Section 31, folios 198-199 verso, scans 391-394; Part D(b), full loop-outer finite actions in type (1,1)
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The boundary augmentation is injected into the actual split-extension homology by odd-degree deck averaging before any section-edge rank argument. The section vertices are full conjugacy classes with explicit transporter cosets.
notes: For an invariant surjective character chi:F->C_m with m odd, the cusp class splits into m/|chi(C)| full section classes. Its m dihedral edges have differences equal to the m boundary vectors, which retain their sole total-sum relation in H1(E_m,F2). The incidence rank forces chi(C)=0 and chi(g) to generate C_m. Brown comparison in the degree-three cover identifies the cusp class specifically as the zero-H1 class. Passing through every odd prime-power character and the zero dyadic first cohomology proves C is contained in the ambient closed commutator subgroup. The finite characteristic group of order 32 proves g has nonzero mod-two abelian image, so its ambient homology class generates the full fixed line. In the two-class case the remaining Brown contribution forces the other fixed subgroup to surject onto every odd cyclic fixed-line quotient; D58's nonzero Bockstein radical supplies the dyadic unit. No full free-basis primitivity, triviality of C, or procyclicity of the other fixed group is inferred.
computational_checks: work/part_c/code/torus_cusp_cycle_d59.py and its adjacent JSON/stdout certificate: exact binary incidence ranks for odd degrees, boundary-module and high cyclic-cohomology dimensions, and every involutive GL2(F2) action on the characteristic group of order 32.
